newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suez Canal cuts tolls for Aqaba-bound wheat.
newsitem.headline: Suez Canal cuts tolls for Aqaba-bound wheat.

text.p: The Suez Canal is offering a discount of 10 percent on transit tolls for wheat cargoes bound for the Jordanian port of Aqaba.
The reduction, which came into effect on Saturday, also applies to the same vessels on their return trip, the Suez Canal Authority (SCA) said in a statement faxed to Reuters on Monday.
To qualify for the reduction "a certificate from Aqaba harbour proving complete discharge of the shipment in the harbour should be submitted," SCA said.
Full tolls must be paid on the day of the first trip until the certificate is produced, it added.
The reduction will be valid for an experimental period of six months, it added.
The SCA last Friday applied another reduction on tolls for containarised cargoes that pass the canal on journeys between the Mediterranean and Jordanian port of Aqaba.
The aim of the reductions is to help the canal compete with routes opened between Aqaba and Israeli ports since the Israeli-Jordanian peace treaty in 1994.

Egypt, which became the first Arab country to make peace with Israel in 1979, fears canal business will drop because of the Israeli-Jordanian peace and shippers using Israel's Mediterranean ports of Haifa and Ashdod for the region.
